title: Establish a plan for the monitoring, safe use and maintenance of equipment implements, technology and infrastructure

lessons.title: Building an asset register and maintenance plan
lessons.html:
Why a plan?

Equipment, implements, technology (such as irrigation controllers, GPS guidance, sensors and computers) and infrastructure (buildings, fences, pipelines, roads, power supply) represent a large share of a farm's capital. Without a plan, maintenance is reactive, breakdowns happen at critical times, safety suffers and assets wear out early.

Step 1: Asset register

List every significant asset with:

  • Asset number, description, make, model and serial number
  • Location and responsible person
  • Purchase date, cost and expected useful life
  • Manufacturer's service requirements
  • Critical rating: how badly a failure would affect operations or safety

Step 2: Determine maintenance requirements

  • Manufacturer's manuals for intervals, lubricants and parts
  • Operating conditions: dust, sand, heavy loads and long hours shorten intervals
  • Legal and safety requirements, such as pressure vessel inspections, electrical installations and lifting equipment
  • History of breakdowns for each asset

Step 3: Choose the maintenance strategy

StrategyWhen to use
Preventive (time or hours based)Engines, gearboxes, pumps, critical machines
Condition-basedWhere wear can be measured: oil analysis, vibration, tyre tread, belt tension
SeasonalPlanters, sprayers, harvesters before and after their season
Run-to-failureCheap, non-critical items with spares in stock

Step 4: Schedule and resources

Draw up a calendar showing when each task is due, avoiding peak periods. Plan workshop capacity, skills, spares, tools and budget. Keep critical spares (filters, belts, nozzles, bearings) in stock before the season.

Step 5: Assign responsibility

Define who does daily checks (operators), routine services (workshop staff), specialist work (dealers or contractors) and who approves and records the work.

lessons.title: Safe use, monitoring and review
lessons.html:
Safe use procedures

The OHS Act 85 of 1993 requires employers to provide and maintain safe plant and machinery and to inform, instruct and train workers. The plan should include:

  • Operator authorisation: only trained, competent and authorised people operate specific machines; keep a register.
  • Safe operating procedures for each machine type: pre-start checks, PTO and guard rules, rollover protection and seatbelts, passengers, slopes, road travel.
  • Lockout procedures for servicing: isolate power, remove keys, release stored energy, tag.
  • PPE requirements for each task.
  • Risk assessments reviewed when equipment or tasks change.
  • Incident reporting and investigation.

Monitoring

  • Daily checklists completed and signed by operators.
  • Hour meter and fuel records for each machine; abnormal fuel use can signal a fault or theft.
  • Inspection schedules for infrastructure: fences, pipelines, dams, roofs, electrical boards.
  • Technology monitoring: software updates, sensor calibration, data backups and battery checks.
  • Job cards for every repair: fault, work done, parts, hours and cost.

Key performance indicators

  • Downtime hours of critical machines
  • Maintenance cost per hour or per hectare
  • Percentage of services done on time
  • Number of breakdowns and incidents

Review and replacement

Review the plan at least yearly and after major breakdowns or incidents. Compare repair costs against the value and remaining life of each asset to decide when to replace. Use the review to update budgets, spares and training.

Communicating the plan

Display schedules in the workshop, brief operators at the start of each season, and make manuals and procedures available in suitable languages.

Key points

  • Start with a complete asset register including critical ratings.
  • Base maintenance on manuals, conditions, history and legal requirements.
  • Match strategy to the asset: preventive, condition-based, seasonal or run-to-failure.
  • Include operator authorisation, lockout and PPE in safe use procedures.
  • Monitor with checklists, job cards and KPIs, and review yearly.
